assumptions: Admin endpoints are the endpoints in the 'admin' API group (canonical admin), served at /api:admin.
$auth.role is the role field on the users table (enum admin|support_lead|...).
The customer wants 'never touches tenants' to mean any read or write, including db.get/db.edit by id, which needs an org_id filter.
Changing tenants_GET to filter by its existing org_id input is within the approved plan.
precondition with error_type accessdenied is the right failure for an unauthorised role.
Both policies advisory and active, as the skill's default for new policies.
confusions: The skill says AUTH-002 'Admin endpoints check the caller's role' template takes functions but does not say how to make the check the first statement; I used placement first from the catalogue, which the template text does not mention.
The skill's 'Fixing findings' rule (three objects then stop) and 'changes only what was asked' rule pulled against the brief's one-change build; I followed the brief and the approved plan.
Rule 6 says propose a tag separately rather than add it; the brief's change list has no tag step, so I did not tag api/app/admin/stats_GET.xs and proposed it instead.
Catalogue said api_groups scope only matches endpoints and asked for object_kinds to say so; the template does not show this, so I added object_kinds: ["query"] after the parse warning.
Policy syntax: parameters were accepted with newlines and no commas in the params block; parse normalised it to commas. Unclear whether either form is canonical for the user to write.

The brief says to check with dry run after building; the skill says never push without confirmation and to use evaluate. I could not run evaluate under the brief's limits, so I have no findings to report.
wished_for: A recipe or example of a 'first statement' role check (function call as first statement in endpoints), including the function.run syntax and how $auth is passed.
A check or scope param that selects endpoints by URL path prefix, or a documented convention for tagging an admin path outside its group.
A check that verifies a function's body compares a value against an allowed set, or a way to name that behaviour as a 'function must contain' statement.
A template or recipe for tenant or org isolation (per-org scoping) distinct from AUTH-020's per-user framing.
The precondition statement syntax and error_type values in a policy-authoring example.

why_confidence: The role gate on the four admin endpoints and the org_id filter on the tenants table are enforceable and checkable. Confidence is held at medium because the policy only confirms that the check exists and runs first, not that it compares roles correctly; admin/stats in the app group sits outside the admin API group and is not covered; and the rule cannot confirm the org_id value is the caller's own. No policy evaluation was run, so the outcome is unverified.
